column1: # The old field of a record (or, with the P: prefix, of a provenance) and the column that holds it: written by hand from
# the table of this repository's qualification store spec, section 3.5, one line per leaf. tools/test_records_db.py reads
# each path's value from the JSON and the column's value with its own SQL, and compares them. It does not use the
# writer's mapping, so a mapping wrong in the writer and the exporter alike (two columns swapped in both) fails here.
# `[]` is an array element. `present`: the column is 1 when the field is present, NULL when absent (the text itself is a
# sentence and is not stored). `presence`: 1 when the JSON object is present, 0 when absent; `presence:<object>`: the
# same, and NULL when <object> is absent.
# Not here: the named values of a map (params, versions, packages, passes, settings), which the tests read by name, and
# the sentences (section 3.5), which no column holds.
